\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക} (upayōgappeṭuttuka)}{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക (upayōgappeṭuttuka)}]{\ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക} (upayōgappeṭuttuka) — to make use of}

\label{lesson:ML-C458-upayogappetuttuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to establish, then the Malayalam for to maintain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക}}
\textbf{\ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക}} — \emph{upayōgappeṭuttuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to make use of\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൻ} \ml{ആ} \ml{അവസരം} \ml{നന്നായി} \ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avan ā avasaraṁ nannāyi upayōgappeṭutti.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He made good use of that opportunity.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തി}, \emph{upayōgappeṭutti}.

A fuller form of \ml{ഉപയോഗിക്കുക}, to use.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക}} (\emph{upayōgappeṭuttuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{upayoga}, \textquotedblleft{}employment, use\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with -\ml{പ്പെടുത്തുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to cause to be\textquotedblright{}, from native \ml{പെടുക} (DEDR 3853): to bring a thing into use.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upayōgappeṭuttuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upayōgappeṭuttuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avan ā avasaraṁ nannāyi upayōgappeṭutti.} — He made good use of that opportunity.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to establish, then the Malayalam for to maintain, then say \emph{upayōgappeṭuttuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഉപയോഗപ്പെടുത്തുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make use of\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക} (viniyōgikkuka)}{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക (viniyōgikkuka)}]{\ml{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക} (viniyōgikkuka) — to allocate funds; to spend}

\label{lesson:ML-C458-viniyogikkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to maintain, then the Malayalam for to make use of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക}} — \emph{viniyōgikkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to allocate funds; to spend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{പഞ്ചായത്ത്} \ml{ആ} \ml{പണം} \ml{കുടിവെള്ളത്തിന്} \ml{വിനിയോഗിച്ചു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pañcāyattŭ ā paṇaṁ kuṭiveḷḷattinŭ viniyōgiccu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The panchayat spent that money on drinking water.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{വിനിയോഗിച്ചു}, \emph{viniyōgiccu}.

Said of funds and powers; people say \ml{ചെലവാക്കുക} for everyday spending.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക}} (\emph{viniyōgikkuka}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{viniyoga}, \textquotedblleft{}apportionment, distribution; employment\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the Malayalam verb ending -\ml{ിക്കുക}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viniyōgikkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viniyōgikkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pañcāyattŭ ā paṇaṁ kuṭiveḷḷattinŭ viniyōgiccu.} — The panchayat spent that money on drinking water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to maintain, then the Malayalam for to make use of, then say \emph{viniyōgikkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വിനിയോഗിക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To allocate funds; to spend\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പാഴാക്കുക} (pāḻākkuka)}{പാഴാക്കുക (pāḻākkuka)}]{\ml{പാഴാക്കുക} (pāḻākkuka) — to waste}

\label{lesson:ML-C458-palakkuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to make use of, then the Malayalam for to allocate funds.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പാഴാക്കുക}}
\textbf{\ml{പാഴാക്കുക}} — \emph{pāḻākkuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to waste\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൻ} \ml{സമയം} \ml{ഒട്ടും} \ml{പാഴാക്കിയില്ല}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avan samayaṁ oṭṭuṁ pāḻākkiyilla.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not waste any time at all.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{പാഴാക്കി}, \emph{pāḻākki}.

\ml{പാഴ്}, waste, with \ml{ആക്കുക}, to make.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പാഴാക്കുക}} (\emph{pāḻākkuka}) is a native Malayalam compound: \ml{പാഴ്}, \textquotedblleft{}an empty place; waste, useless\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4110), and \ml{ആക്കുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 333): to make a thing useless.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāḻākkuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāḻākkuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avan samayaṁ oṭṭuṁ pāḻākkiyilla.} — He did not waste any time at all.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to make use of, then the Malayalam for to allocate funds, then say \emph{pāḻākkuka} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പാഴാക്കുക} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To waste\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വായ്പ} (vāypa)}{വായ്പ (vāypa)}]{\ml{വായ്പ} (vāypa) — a loan}

\label{lesson:ML-C458-vaypa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to allocate funds, then the Malayalam for to waste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വായ്പ}}
\textbf{\ml{വായ്പ}} — \emph{vāypa} — \textquotedblleft{}a loan\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{വീട്} \ml{പണിയാൻ} \ml{അവർ} \ml{ബാങ്കിൽ} \ml{നിന്ന്} \ml{വായ്പ} \ml{എടുത്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vīṭŭ paṇiyān avar bāṅkil ninnŭ vāypa eṭuttu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They took a loan from the bank to build a house.
\end{quote}

A bank loan is \ml{വായ്പ}; a private debt is usually \ml{കടം}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വായ്പ}} (\emph{vāypa}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 5355 lists Malayalam \emph{vāypa}, \textquotedblleft{}a loan\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{vāyppai}, \textquotedblleft{}a debt\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāypa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vāypa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vīṭŭ paṇiyān avar bāṅkil ninnŭ vāypa eṭuttu.} — They took a loan from the bank to build a house.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to allocate funds, then the Malayalam for to waste, then say \emph{vāypa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വായ്പ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A loan\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്യുക} (sambhāvana ceyyuka)}{സംഭാവന ചെയ്യുക (sambhāvana ceyyuka)}]{\ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്യുക} (sambhāvana ceyyuka) — to donate; to contribute}

\label{lesson:ML-C458-sambhavana-ceyyuka}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for to waste, then the Malayalam for a loan.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}}
\textbf{\ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}} — \emph{sambhāvana ceyyuka} — \textquotedblleft{}to donate; to contribute\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{നാട്ടുകാർ} \ml{ആശുപത്രിക്ക്} \ml{പണം} \ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്തു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nāṭṭukār āśupatrikkŭ paṇaṁ sambhāvana ceytu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The local people donated money to the hospital.
\end{quote}

Past: \ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്തു}, \emph{sambhāvana ceytu}.

The noun \ml{സംഭാവന} is a donation, a contribution.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{സംഭാവന} \ml{ചെയ്യുക}} (\emph{sambhāvana ceyyuka}) is a phrase verb built on \ml{സംഭാവന}, \textquotedblleft{}a donation\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{saṁbhāvanā}, \textquotedblleft{}bringing together; honour, respect\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with \ml{ചെയ്യുക}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sambhāvana ceyyuka}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sambhāvana ceyyuka}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāṭṭukār āśupatrikkŭ paṇaṁ sambhāvana ceytu.} — The local people donated money to the hospital.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for to waste, then the Malayalam for a loan, then say \emph{sambhāvana ceyyuka} again
\end{itemize}
